summary: Sprint KE-003 backend regression executed via new /app/backend/tests/test_ke003_certification_workspace.py — 4/6 PASS, 1 FAIL (needs-review missing 'first_anomaly' field), 1 SKIP (review-entities endpoint not exposed). UI Playwright test could not complete past login: form filled correctly but POST /api/auth/login flow ended back at /auth/login with 401s — likely a Playwright-side cookie/session persistence issue rather than a real auth bug (manual login + previous iterations 210/211 verified login works). Therefore P0-1..P0-10 UI flows were NOT re-validated in this iteration and should be re-run by main agent or next testing pass. Backend KE-003 endpoints are mostly healthy: validation-summary kpi block has all 8 required keys for both RIVA1920 and ARBI; RIVA KPI is non-zero (regression OK for KE-002); failure-context returns full 7-key shape on a real failed RIVA doc; backfill-semantic-events returns {ok, documents_processed, documents_skipped, totals} and is idempotent across 2 sequential POSTs. ONE BACKEND CONTRACT BUG: GET /api/knowledge/catalog-sets/{id}/needs-review?type=designer_ambiguous returns ['entities','count','filter'] but the documented contract requires 'first_anomaly' — confirmed on BOTH RIVA (count=26) and ARBI (count=14). This affects P0-1 deep-link flow because handleDeepLink relies on focus=first_anomaly_id from the API.

critical.issue: Response is missing the 'first_anomaly' field documented in KE-003 contract. Verified on RIVA (a1b8cfac, designer_ambiguous, count=26) and ARBI (00e33d7f, designer_ambiguous, count=14) — both return {entities, count, filter} only. Frontend P0-1 deep-link toast 'Apertura prima anomalia: <id>' depends on this field; without it, focus query-param falls back to first entities[0].id or null.

minor.issue: Endpoint not exposed (404/missing) — caused TestApplyCorrectionImpact to skip. apply-correction itself was not directly verifiable in this run; iteration 210 verified it works end-to-end via the UI 'Approva validazione' flow.

integration_issues.issue: Navigation to /login redirects to /auth/login, form fields fill, submit click does not transition to /inspirations; URL stays at /auth/login with multiple 401/403 console errors during the flow. Manual login via curl POST /api/auth/login works (returns session.access_token). Investigate cookie/CSRF handling in Playwright context — possibly httpOnly cookie not surviving across the post-submit redirect chain in headless context.

critical_code_review_comments: needs-review response is missing first_anomaly — contract drift. Cheapest fix: in router after computing entities list, return first_anomaly = entities[0] if entities else None.

ReviewWorkspaceV3.jsx (per problem statement at L171/368/549/630) intentionally keeps BOTH legacy AIValidation rw-approve-{entity_id} buttons AND the new in-Inspector rw-cert-* CTAs — this is documented but creates a duplicated certification surface; long-term consider hiding the legacy approve from val-cards to enforce the single inspector flow and reduce cognitive load.
P0-9 UNISCI takes a raw entity_id from a text input — no entity search / suggestions UI. Recommend a typeahead lookup against existing entities of the same kind to avoid users guessing UUIDs.
P0-10 RIFIUTA uses window.confirm() — not stylable, breaks the Blueprint Chameleon aesthetic. Replace with an in-app confirmation modal that matches the dark glassmorphism design language.

Knowledge Impact computation: apply-correction request body sends impact={all zeros} and trusts backend to compute real values — good separation. Ensure _compute_real_impact in /app/backend/routers/review_workspace_v3.py covers scope='brand' (cross-catalog impact across the brand's other catalog sets) — that's the most complex case and is the easiest to regress.

rca of the issue: needs-review missing first_anomaly RCA: The backend computes the entities[] list correctly (verified count=26 on RIVA designer_ambiguous, count=14 on ARBI) but the serializer in extraction_jobs.py returns only {entities, count, filter}. The KE-003 spec requires {entities, count, filter, first_anomaly} where first_anomaly = entities[0] (or highest-priority entity) to power the deep-link focus query param (?focus=<entity_id>). One-line fix in the route handler: `return {..., 'first_anomaly': entities[0] if entities else None}`. This also affects the toast 'Apertura prima anomalia: <id>' which currently must derive the id from entities[0] client-side, masking the contract drift.
